entry.evidence: Yet, there is a long-standing controversy whether siderite-copper mineral deposits actually relate to mineralizing processes of Variscan or Alpine age in the Western Carpathians.

sequences.source_document: Publisher XML full text (jats_text) checked against the published PDF

steps.action: Pose the question of whether the Ni–Co(–Cu) mineralizations of the Western Carpathians are of Variscan or Alpine age.
steps.quote: there is a long-standing controversy whether siderite-copper mineral deposits actually relate to mineralizing processes of Variscan or Alpine age

steps.action: List the published rival ages and origins for the Kolba occurrence and for similar deposits: syngenetic Variscan, Variscan with Alpine remobilization, epigenetic Alpine, Permian, and Cretaceous.
steps.quote: were considered to be syngenetic-stratiform of Variscan age, Variscan with Alpine remobilization, or epigenetic of Alpine age

steps.action: Design the test as absolute geochronology of the ore minerals themselves (Ni–Co arsenides and sulfarsenides) rather than of host or gangue phases.
steps.quote: To resolve this ambiguity, absolute geochronology directly targeting minerals of economic interest (i.e., sulfides, sulfarsenides, or arsenides) is ideal.

steps.action: Adopt the recently developed Re–Os chronometer for cobaltite, gersdorffite and rammelsbergite from other groups' and the authors' earlier work.
steps.quote: recent development of the 187Re–187Os chronometer has seen its application to sulfarsenides and arsenides

steps.action: Determine the Kolba paragenesis (albite-carbonate, krutovite to zoned gersdorffite, later Cu–Bi minerals) from hand specimens, reflected-light microscopy and electron microprobe analyses of dump samples.
steps.quote: The paragenetic sequence, as determined from observation of hand specimens, polished sections in polarized-light microscopy, and electron microprobe, is shown in Fig. 2.

steps.action: Select Kolba sample KO-4 for dating on the basis of its standard paragenesis, representative composition and high Re content.
steps.quote: In light of its standard paragenetic association, a mineral composition matching the main mineralization type described here, and its high Re content

steps.action: Check the purity of the hand-picked gersdorffite separate by powder X-ray diffraction.
steps.quote: consists of single-phase gersdorffite as confirmed by powder X-ray diffraction

steps.action: Describe the Čierna Lehota epigenetic Ni–Co–As ores: colloform intergrowths of Co-rich and later Ni–Fe skutterudite with pararammelsbergite, followed by late sulfarsenides and Bi–Cu phases.
steps.quote: consist of fine-grained intergrowths of early skutterudite [(Co,Ni,Fe)As3] and pararammelsbergite (NiAs2)

steps.action: Date mixed skutterudite-pararammelsbergite separates from Čierna Lehota because the phases cannot be separated; XRD shows minor gersdorffite and arsenopyrite.
steps.quote: In light of their predominance, Re–Os dating was carried out on mixtures dominated by skutterudite and pararammelsbergite.

steps.action: Compute the Re–Os model age of gersdorffite KO-4 (238.2 ± 1.0 Ma), switching to a mixed double-Os spike after an initial analysis showed almost no common Os.
steps.quote: a model age of 238.2 ± 1.0 Ma using the mixed double-Os spike

steps.action: Monitor measurement quality with in-house Re and Os standards, a total procedural blank, and the Henderson molybdenite age reference material (Methods only).
steps.quote: Measurement quality was monitored by measurements of in-house Re and Os standards over the analysis period

steps.action: Regress four Čierna Lehota analyses, including a replicate of CL-1, into a model 1 isochron (238.2 ± 12.7 Ma, MSWD 0.95, initial 187Os/188Os 0.90 ± 0.01).
steps.quote: yielding a 4-point model 1 isochron regression (mean square weighted deviates, MSWD = 0.95) with a date of 238.2 ± 12.7 Ma (2σ)

steps.action: Argue from the absence of cross-cutting relationships and from the colloform textures that the mineralization was a single rapid pulse, so the isochron dates mineralization.
steps.quote: We interpret that the Ni–Co–As mineralization formed in a single hydrothermal pulse

steps.action: Support the Čierna Lehota isochron age with the independent gersdorffite model age from the other deposit, Kolba.
steps.quote: This interpretation is further supported by the Re–Os model age of gersdorffite at Kolba.

steps.action: Infer a crustal Os source from the radiogenic initial ratio, and infer metabasic rocks as the Ni–Co source from cited host-rock compositions.
steps.quote: The initial 187Os/188Os of 0.90 ± 0.01 points to interaction of the fluids with crustal lithologies

steps.action: Compare the ~238 Ma ages with the cited magmatic and sedimentary record of Middle–Late Triassic extension during the incipient opening of the Meliata ocean.
steps.quote: An extensional setting in Middle-Late Triassic (Plašienka 27) related to the incipient stage of the opening of the Meliata ocean is documented

steps.action: Extend the interpretation to other small hydrothermal deposits using cited Triassic Pb–Pb model ages, and call for more Re–Os dating.
steps.quote: may have created a number of small hydrothermal deposits, not only those investigated in this work

steps.action: Keep the claim that both Ni–Co mineralizations are Middle Triassic (Ladinian) and tied to extension and fluid flow during the opening of the Meliata ocean.
steps.quote: We conclude that studied Ni–Co mineralizations are related to an extensional tectonic regime and hydrothermal fluid flow

end.claim: Ni–Co mineralization at Ľubietová-Kolba and Čierna Lehota formed at ca. 238 Ma (Middle Triassic, Ladinian) from crustally sourced hydrothermal fluids, linked to extension during the incipient opening of the Meliata ocean.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the Re–Os model age of gersdorffite KO-4 and the concordant skutterudite-pararammelsbergite isochron there would be no Middle Triassic date to link to the Meliata opening.

gates.evidence: Action: the dating was directed by the question of Variscan versus Alpine age and its cited rivals (§1 ¶1–2), not by one stated hypothesis. Claim: the dates could have fallen in the Variscan or Cretaceous windows, so the age was exposed to failure. The Meliata link was not tested against alternatives; it rests on coincidence with cited extensional records (§5.2 ¶1). Registration: nothing is reported as fixed before the data; the spike choice was adapted after initial analyses (§3.3 ¶3).

imports.item: Negative thermal ionization mass spectrometry (Thermo Triton) for Re and Os isotopes
Carius tube digestion and solvent extraction / microdistillation of Os
Wavelength-dispersive electron microprobe with ZAF correction
Powder X-ray diffraction to document separate purity
NIST Reference Material 8599 Henderson molybdenite as age standard

limits: Sub-claims at different statuses: the ages (238.2 ± 1.0 Ma model age; 238.2 ± 12.7 Ma isochron) are estimate_with_resolution; the crustal Os source and metabasic Ni–Co source are best_explanation from the initial ratio and cited host-rock compositions; the Meliata link (headline) is best_explanation by coincidence with cited extensional records and is not tested against alternatives. The paper never explicitly excludes the cited Variscan, Permian or Cretaceous rivals; their exclusion is implied by the date (inference). The Kolba date rests on a single sample (KO-4). The isochron has four points, two of them analyses of the same CL-1 separate, so only three separates are represented (inference from Table 2). The dated separates at Čierna Lehota are mineral mixtures with minor gersdorffite and arsenopyrite. All samples come from dumps without in-situ structural context. The younger Cu–Bi mineralization is not dated. The reasons for choosing KO-4 among four Kolba samples, and CL-1, CL-2 and CL-8 among ten Čierna Lehota samples, are only partly given. Preliminary Re analyses were made by another laboratory (acknowledgments, p. 628), and the paper does not report how they were used. No review file was supplied, so changes made in review cannot be coded.

disagreements.target: Ilavský (1976); Varček (1978): Kolba Cu–Ni–Co occurrence as syngenetic Variscan, Variscan with Alpine remobilization, or epigenetic Alpine
disagreements.support: Direct Re–Os dating of gersdorffite at Kolba gives a Middle Triassic age outside the Variscan and Cretaceous Alpine windows, though the paper does not state the rejection explicitly.
disagreements.quote: To resolve this ambiguity, absolute geochronology directly targeting minerals of economic interest (i.e., sulfides, sulfarsenides, or arsenides) is ideal.

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Conventional 185Re + 190Os spike (used in the initial analysis and for the CL samples)
alternatives_considered.reason: Initial analysis showed little common Os, with 187Os* above 99.6% of the Os measured

alternatives_considered.chosen: Mixed skutterudite-pararammelsbergite separates at Čierna Lehota
alternatives_considered.reason: Owing to the fine-grained nature of the arsenides and sulfarsenides, it is impossible to separate the individual minerals

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Other Kolba samples among the subset of four
alternatives_considered.reason: Standard paragenetic association, composition matching the main mineralization type, high Re content (264 ng g−1)

alternatives_considered.chosen: Metabasic rocks as the source of Ni and Co
alternatives_considered.reason: Metabasic rocks average 152 ppm Ni and 46 ppm Co versus 5 ppm Ni and 0.8 ppm Co in the carbonaceous rocks
